beats.description: Pre-dawn, Noor is scrolling social media and stops on a thread about the Halloway West cake — ordinary comment-section noise that snags her attention anyway. She opens a Diagnostic Glass session on Tomas Vale's Float-ID meaning only to confirm a single fact: one filed correction or more than one. The sealed document she finds (case AST-2291-RV-114, authorization AUTH-COR-88214-VEND, filed at a different building than the one she expected) is a second correction on his identity that appears nowhere in the institutions or corrections ledgers. She widens the query cross-department to three more sealed cases, logging a WARN_CROSS_DEPARTMENT_LOGGED flag she's honest with herself about, and blows past the stopping point she set for herself at the start.

Mote's ambient monitoring registers the shape of Noor's session as it happens — one Float-ID widening to four sealed documents across three authorizing bodies in about twenty minutes — without surfacing what she actually found. He recognizes the originating Float-ID as the one underneath B's open case and notes it for the record, more so no one can later say he missed it than because he's decided yet what to do about it.

Reading his own flag back, Mote decides: tell B, but only what the query log actually supports — scope and timing, not a finding he doesn't have and won't invent. He weighs and rejects the faster option of asking Noor first so he could hand B something tidier, on the grounds that it would trade her privacy for his own convenience.

B receives Mote's filtered notice: Noor pulled sealed records tied to Tomas Vale's Float-ID before dawn, widening cross-department inside twenty minutes. It reaches him as scope and timing only — something surfaced near his case, from someone who hasn't told him what.

B reads the notice and separates the two things he's actually reacting to: that it's his case she went into without telling him, and that she was awake at four in the morning to do it. He skips the formal Dev-to-Dev channel and just texts her — asking what she found, but mostly asking if she's all right.
